oil.summary: Crude markets are caught in a tug-of-war between geopolitical risk and bearish supply dynamics. Brent edged up 0.57% to $92.97 while WTI was near flat at $85.65, but both remain deeply underwater on the month — down 15% and 17% respectively — reflecting demand-side pressure. The Strait of Hormuz remains the dominant headline risk: Iran reports three tankers struck by mines and a third U.S. carrier has arrived in the region, keeping a risk premium embedded in Brent. Simultaneously, Russian crude exports hit a four-month high above 30 million barrels as Ukrainian drone strikes displaced oil from domestic refineries to export channels. Trump's public warning to Zelensky to cease refinery attacks adds a political wildcard. Refined products sold off sharply, with RBOB down 1.65% and heating oil off 2.79%. CME options imply a 77% probability of an OPEC cut at the May 2027 meeting.
drivers: Strait of Hormuz escalation: three tankers mined, third U.S. carrier deployed, Iran escalating threats — supporting Brent risk premium
Russian crude exports surge to four-month high as Ukrainian strikes redirect barrels from refineries to tankers, adding supply to seaborne markets
Sharp selloff in refined products (RBOB -1.65%, heating oil -2.79%) and deep month-on-month losses across the complex signal underlying demand weakness; OPEC cut odds at 77% for May

gas.summary: Henry Hub rebounded 2.27% on the day to $3.193/MMBtu, partially recovering from a weekly loss of 3.12%, while the month-on-month gain of 4.41% suggests some structural support. In Europe, TTF bounced to approximately €85.48/MWh (+0.86%), recovering from a reported 7% drop on Monday as Hormuz-related risks resurfaced — tanker strikes in the strait and a drone alarm at an Iraqi gas field kept traders on edge. Russia launched 116 attacks on Ukraine's energy and gas sector over the past week, adding supply-side anxiety in Europe. Reliance Industries' announced $1.6 billion investment in 100 Indian biogas plants is a medium-term structural note. News flow for this sector is relatively limited beyond the Hormuz/Ukraine supply-risk thread.
drivers: TTF recovery from Monday's 7% drop driven by renewed Strait of Hormuz vessel attacks and drone incident at Iraqi gas field
Russia's 116 attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure over the past week sustain European supply-security concerns
Henry Hub +2.27% intraday bounce, though still down 3.12% on the week — headline support from geopolitical risk rather than fresh fundamental catalyst

power.summary: EU carbon EUAs traded marginally lower at $83.13 (-0.16%), broadly flat on the week (-0.89%) but up 1.83% on the month, suggesting modest structural support in the absence of a strong directional catalyst. TTF's +0.86% session gain feeds into European power generation costs at the margin. The EU's new sanctions package targeting Russian banks, energy firms, and offshore traders could tighten Russian energy revenue flows, though the direct power-market impact is unclear from available data. Japan's proposed 'Asian IEA' and 'Power Gulf Initiative' reflect growing import-side coordination pressure among Asian consumers. China's milestone crewed flight of an all-electric aircraft is a long-horizon demand-destruction data point. Dedicated power-price data is not available in today's feed; the EUA and TTF moves are the primary tradeable signals.
drivers: EU EUA near flat at $83.13 with marginal monthly support (+1.83%); TTF recovery adds modest upward pressure on carbon-intensive power generation costs
New EU sanctions targeting Russian energy firms and offshore traders could incrementally tighten Russian supply pipelines into European markets
Japan's proposed Asian energy stockpiling task force signals structural shift in demand-side coordination among major crude and LNG importers
